name: Catechol
note: Catechol moieties are PAINS frequent hitters; metal chelation + auto-oxidation. Cefiderocol exception uses this intentionally as a siderophore.

name: Quinone
note: Para-quinones are reactive Michael acceptors → covalent adducts to thiols/amines, redox cycling toxicity.

name: Aryl-aldehyde (PAINS)
note: Salicylaldehyde-like motifs flag in PAINS filters; can form Schiff bases with biogenic amines.

name: Hydrazine
note: Hydrazines (N-N single bond) are mutagenic/hepatotoxic in many cases. Linezolid's oxazolidinone N is exempt (in-ring).

name: Acyl halide
note: Acyl halides hydrolyze rapidly; never appear in marketed drugs.

name: Epoxide
note: 3-membered O-ring; alkylates DNA/proteins. Use only as a designed warhead (e.g. fosfomycin).

name: Aziridine
note: 3-membered N-ring; alkylating agent (mitomycin C class warhead).

name: Michael acceptor (α,β-unsaturated carbonyl)
note: Prone to thiol addition; common false positive in HTS. Some kinase inhibitors use this as a designed covalent warhead.

name: Sulfonate ester
note: Mesylate/tosylate-class esters are alkylating agents (mutagens).

name: Thiocyanate
note: Reactive electrophile; promiscuous binder.

name: Aromatic-N-oxide
note: Some N-oxides are bioactivated to genotoxins (e.g. 4-nitroquinoline N-oxide).

name: Disulfide
note: Reduces in cell to thiols; promiscuous.

name: Crown/macrocycle (large ring)
note: Large rings often have low membrane permeability; macrolide antibiotics (erythromycin, azithromycin) are intentional exceptions.

name: Isothiocyanate
note: Thiol-trapping electrophile; common in mustard oil (allyl-NCS).

name: 1,2-dihydroxybenzene oxidation hazard
note: Hydroquinone oxidizes to benzoquinone (Michael acceptor); same lineage as catechol issue.

name: Aliphatic primary amine on benzylic C (toxicophore)
note: Benzylamines are MAO substrates (amphetamine-class); CNS effects expected.

name: Pentavalent P (phosphate)
note: Phosphates have very low passive permeability; viable as nucleotide prodrugs only.

name: Trichloromethyl
note: CCl3 group → trichlorocarbon radical (chloroform-class hepatotoxicity).

name: β-lactam ring
note: Required pharmacophore for penicillins / cephalosporins / carbapenems / monobactams. NOT a structural alert; flagged here for visibility.

name: Quinolone core
note: Fluoroquinolone scaffold; binds DNA gyrase (gyrA, parC). Adding F at C6 boosts activity 4-10×.
